summary: Defines the value "application" for the vCard KIND property so a vCard can represent a software application. A contact card can describe a program as well as a person or organization.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds the application value to the vCard KIND property. A vCard can then describe a software application, including a server, online service, or automated bot.

questions: how to represent software in vcard
what does application mean in vcard kind
how can a vcard describe software
subtitle: The vCard KIND value application represents a software application.

tldr.problem: The vCard KIND property had no value for representing a software application.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines application as a KIND value and describes how vCard properties can represent the application and associated people or organizations.
tldr.outcome: vCards can represent software applications such as servers, online services, and automated bots.

today: RFC 6473 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Application KIND Value
sections.content:
vCard version 4 defines the KIND property to state what type of entity a vCard represents. Existing values include individual, organization, group, and location. The working group removed a broader thing value and expected extensions to define narrower types.

This RFC defines the narrower application value for software applications.
sections.plainLanguage: The KIND property labels what a vCard describes. This extension adds a label for software.

sections.title: What an Application vCard Describes
sections.content:
An application may be a server, an online service such as a chat room, or an automated software bot. Its vCard properties may describe the application itself, the organization or person making it available, or the person or role maintaining it.

For properties about the application itself, work and home TYPE values do not make sense. The RFC lists useful properties such as FN, URL, ADR, GEO, TEL, EMAIL, and TZ, and says a more detailed application taxonomy is out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The card can describe the software, its provider, or its maintainer. A program itself does not have a home or workplace.

sections.title: Example, Registration, and Security
sections.content:
The example is a vCard for an XMPP instant-messaging service, with KIND set to application. IANA added application to the vCard 4 property-value registry for use with KIND.

The RFC does not expect this use to introduce security considerations beyond those that apply to vCards generally.
sections.plainLanguage: The example shows a contact card for an online messaging service. The new value is registered for the KIND property.
